title: Australia Joins Gulf War Coalition Against Iraq
notes: Three naval vessels deployed from August 1990. Confirmed as largest deployment since Vietnam.

title: Hawke-Keating Leadership Transition Reshapes Labor
notes: Keating defeated Hawke 56-51 on 19 December 1991. Eight years as Treasurer correct.

title: Mabo Decision Overturns Terra Nullius Doctrine
notes: High Court ruled 3 June 1992 in Mabo v Queensland (No 2), rejecting terra nullius.

title: Native Title Act Gives Legislative Effect to Mabo
notes: Native Title Act 1993 passed by Keating government, commenced 1 January 1994.

title: Keating Wins Surprise 1993 Federal Election
notes: Labor won fifth consecutive term. Hewson's GST-centred Fightback! platform defeated. Surprise result confirmed.

title: APEC Summit in Osaka Advances Australia-Asia Integration
notes: APEC Osaka summit held November 1995. Keating was key architect of APEC summitry.

title: Howard Coalition Government Wins Landslide Victory
notes: Coalition won 75 seats in March 1996, ending 13 years of Labor. Howard served over 11 years.

title: Port Arthur Massacre Triggers Gun Law Reform
notes: 35 killed 28 April 1996. National Firearms Agreement enacted within weeks. Over 650,000 firearms collected in buyback.

title: Bringing Them Home Report on Stolen Generations Released
notes: Report tabled 26 May 1997 by HREOC. Howard government declined formal apology.

title: Wik Legislation Amends Native Title Framework
notes: Native Title Amendment Act 1998 passed July 1998. Wik decision (1996) held coexistence; amendments criticised as weakening native title.

title: Republic Referendum Defeated Despite Majority Support
notes: 54.87% voted No (rounds to 55%). Model was parliamentary appointment not direct election — event description is correct on this point.

title: Australia Leads INTERFET Peacekeeping Force in East Timor
notes: INTERFET deployed 20 September 1999, commanded by Australian Major General Cosgrove. Largest deployment since Vietnam.

title: Sydney Hosts Summer Olympic Games
notes: Sydney 2000 widely praised. Cathy Freeman won gold in 400m, carried both flags as symbol of reconciliation.

title: Goods and Services Tax Introduced
notes: 10% GST commenced 1 July 2000. Most significant tax reform in decades. Central issue of 1998 election.

title: Tampa Affair Transforms Immigration Policy
notes: MV Tampa carrying 433 rescued asylum seekers; military deployed; Pacific Solution of offshore detention on Nauru followed.

title: Australia Invokes ANZUS Treaty After September 11 Attacks
notes: First-ever ANZUS invocation, three days after 9/11. SAS troops committed to Afghanistan under Operation Enduring Freedom.

title: Bali Bombings Kill 88 Australians
notes: 12 October 2002; 202 total killed including exactly 88 Australians; Jemaah Islamiyah responsible.

title: Australia Joins Iraq Invasion as Coalition Partner
notes: ~2,000 troops committed without UN authorisation; anti-war protests occurred domestically.

title: Australia-US Free Trade Agreement Enters Force
notes: AUSFTA was signed in May 2004 but entered into force on 1 January 2005. Year-off by 1 for the entry-into-force claim.

title: Indian Ocean Tsunami Response Mobilises Australian Aid
notes: Tsunami struck 26 December 2004 but Australia's $1 billion aid pledge was announced in January 2005. Major response event belongs to 2005, not 2004.

title: Cronulla Riots Expose Ethnic Tensions in Sydney
notes: Riots began 11 December 2005 in Cronulla between Anglo-Australian and Middle Eastern heritage youth. Emergency powers and national debate followed.

title: WorkChoices Industrial Relations Reform Enacted
notes: Workplace Relations Amendment (Work Choices) Act passed November 2005. Major union protests; central issue in 2007 election.

title: Kevin Rudd Leads Labor to Power Ending Howard Era
notes: Rudd won 24 November 2007. Howard lost Bennelong to Maxine McKew. Climate action, education, Iraq withdrawal were key planks.

title: National Apology to Stolen Generations Delivered
notes: Rudd delivered formal apology 13 February 2008, first order of business in parliament. Passed unanimously.

title: Global Financial Crisis Tests Australian Economy
notes: Australia avoided recession. Stimulus packages totalled ~$52.4 billion (event says 'over 50 billion' — correct). Chinese demand and stimulus both credited.

title: Black Saturday Bushfires Kill 173 in Victoria
notes: 7 February 2009; exactly 173 killed; over 2,000 homes destroyed; Royal Commission followed.

title: Gillard Replaces Rudd as Australia's First Female PM
notes: Gillard sworn in 24 June 2010. Labor dissatisfaction over shelved emissions trading scheme was cited trigger. First female PM confirmed.

title: Hung Parliament Forces Minority Government
notes: August 2010 — first hung parliament since 1940. Gillard formed minority government with Greens and independents.

title: Mining Tax Legislation Passed Amid Industry Opposition
notes: MRRT passed November 2011 on iron ore and coal. Repealed 2014. Revenue far below projections.

title: Carbon Pricing Mechanism Takes Effect
notes: Clean Energy Act 2011 commenced 1 July 2012 at $23/tonne. Coalition campaigned relentlessly on repeal.

title: Abbott Coalition Wins Election on Anti-Carbon Tax Platform
notes: Coalition won September 2013. Rudd returned to Labor leadership three months prior (June 2013). Abbott's platform was repealing carbon tax and stopping boats.

title: Carbon Tax Repealed by Abbott Government
notes: Senate repealed 17 July 2014. Australia was first country to abolish a functioning carbon price.

title: Lindt Cafe Siege in Sydney
notes: 15-16 December 2014; 18 hostages; 2 hostages killed plus perpetrator. Counter-terrorism review followed.

title: Turnbull Ousts Abbott in Liberal Leadership Challenge
notes: Turnbull defeated Abbott 54-44 on 14 September 2015. Cited economic leadership and 30 consecutive Newspoll losses.

title: China-Australia Free Trade Agreement Enters Force
notes: ChAFTA entered into force 20 December 2015. China confirmed as Australia's largest trading partner.

title: Same-Sex Marriage Legalised After Postal Survey
notes: 61.6% voted Yes in November 2017. Marriage Act amended in December 2017.

title: Dual Citizenship Crisis Disqualifies Multiple Parliamentarians
notes: Section 44 crisis; 15 politicians resigned or ruled ineligible; by-elections and resignations across major parties and crossbench.

title: Morrison Replaces Turnbull After Leadership Spill
notes: Morrison defeated Dutton 45-40 on 24 August 2018. No PM had served a full term since Howard.

title: Foreign Interference Laws Target Covert Influence
notes: National Security Legislation Amendment (Espionage and Foreign Interference) Act passed June 2018. Widely attributed to Chinese influence concerns.

title: Morrison Wins Surprise Federal Election Victory
notes: Coalition won May 2019 defying all polling. Queensland result key. Shorten resigned Labor leadership.

title: Black Summer Bushfires Begin Unprecedented Fire Season
notes: Season began September 2019; 24 million hectares burned (event states 18M — understated but not year-wrong or materially false); 33 direct deaths; ~3 billion animals affected.

title: COVID-19 Border Closures and Economic Response
notes: Near-total international travel ban. JobKeeper total cost ~$130 billion (event says 'exceeding 90 billion' — conservative undercount). Supported over 3.5 million workers confirmed.

title: China Imposes Trade Sanctions on Australian Exports
notes: 80.5% barley tariff (event rounds to 80%); wine tariffs exceeded 200%. Followed Australia's COVID inquiry call.

title: Brereton Report Reveals War Crimes in Afghanistan
notes: Released 19 November 2020. 39 unlawful killings by 25 personnel. Criminal referrals and reassessment of special forces culture followed.

title: AUKUS Security Pact Announced With US and UK
notes: Announced 15 September 2021. Centred on nuclear-powered submarines. France recalled ambassadors from Australia and US.

title: French Submarine Contract Cancelled in AUKUS Pivot
notes: Attack-class programme terminated; France recalled ambassadors and called it a betrayal. Contract value reported as $40-90 billion AUD across sources.

title: Albanese Labor Government Elected Ending Coalition Rule
notes: May 2022; ended nine years of Coalition government. Record teal independents won safe Liberal seats on climate and integrity platforms.

title: Eastern Australia Floods Cause Billions in Damage
notes: Confirmed deaths were 24, not 22 as stated. Insured losses exceeded $5 billion — correct. Death count is materially wrong.

title: Voice to Parliament Referendum Defeated
notes: 39.9% Yes, defeated nationally and in all six states. Significant setback for Indigenous recognition.

title: AUKUS Submarine Pathway Details Announced
notes: San Diego announcement March 2023. Virginia-class SSNs, then SSN-AUKUS. Total cost $286-386 billion AUD (event says 'exceeded 360 billion' — within the reported range).

title: China Lifts Barley Tariffs as Diplomatic Relations Thaw
notes: 80.5% barley tariff removed effective 5 August 2023. Followed Albanese government diplomatic engagement.

title: China Removes Wine Tariffs Completing Trade Normalisation
notes: Wine tariffs (up to 218.4%) lifted 29 March 2024. Last major trade barrier from the 2020 campaign removed.
